title: Contribute: record a walk, share it safely

questions.question: How can I contribute?
questions.answer: Record a station walk at nyc.design-bakery.com/record. The page opens the back camera, records video with motion, heading and location, and lets you mark Sign, Stairs and Elevator as you pass them. One recorded walk gives a route's checkpoints, levels and distances.

questions.question: What happens to my recording?
questions.answer: It saves to your phone first, and a Send step submits the walk in one tap. Nothing a rider records is published without their agreement, and video is not published until faces are blurred. Raw footage stays private.

sources.title: Product design document, design rules for rider walks

questions.question: What leaves my phone?
questions.answer: For sign reading, one camera frame when you ask the app to read a sign; the server passes it to the model and does not keep it. Recordings are saved to the phone; submitting a walk is a separate, explicit step.

sources.title: GeoAI hackathon write-up, what leaves the phone

questions.question: Do I need special hardware?
questions.answer: No. A phone browser is enough: the recorder uses the browser's own MediaRecorder, motion, orientation, location and wake-lock APIs. A barometer helps find elevator rides; browsers without one still record video, motion and marks. A native barometer app is planned.

questions.question: Can I contribute code?
questions.answer: Yes. The project is open source on GitHub. The format checker, converter and cleanup functions have tests, and the contribution loop is written out on issue #186. New York has 472 stations; riders walk through all of them every day.

questions.question: Why does one walk matter?
questions.answer: One walk gives the signs in order, the levels from the barometer and the distances from the step count for a route. That is how the project scales to 472 stations without modelling each one by hand.
